1  01 08 15  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 14.01.2023.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 14.01.2023 at about 9.00 p.m., petitioner was traveling as a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336, which was driven by its driver at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, on NH-44 road, at Maruru cross, Rapthadu Mandal,
dashed against the road side divider.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down from the seat and sustained multiple all over the body.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Anantapur, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter petitioner was shifted to Omega Multi Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, Conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent being the owner cum internal insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notice, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition as false and contended that the petition is neither maintainable in law nor on facts and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

This respondent further submitted that, on the date and time of the alleged accident in question was on its schedule trip from Bangalore to Ananthapur and the bus was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding on Bangalore-Ananthapur main road at Maruru cross at that point of time a motorcyclist abruptly darted the main road from the cross road, observing the same the driver of the bus, in order to avoid the bus being dashed against the motorcycle immediately stopped the bus and which has resulted in the minor incident.
But no passengers of the bus sustained injuries.
As such, for the alleged incident unknown motorcyclist was wholly and solely responsible but the driver of the bus in question was no way responsible.
However, the petitioner and police was unable to tract out the motorcycle and falsely implicated the bus in question.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 14.01.2023 at about 09.00 p.m., when the petitioner was a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336 when the said bus reached on NH-44 road, at Maruru cross, Rapthadu mandal, at that time the driver of the said bus driven the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules and dashed to the road side divider and caused the accident and as a result, petitioner sustained injuries as alleged by him?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15 and examined Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.16 and Ex.P.17 and closed their side.
On the other hand, respondent examine two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
8.
ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15.

3 Card.
10.

On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 14.01.2023 at about 9.00 p.m.,
petitioner was traveling as a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336, which was driven by its driver at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, on NH-44 road, at Maruru cross, Rapthadu Mandal, dashed against the road side divider.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down from the seat and sustained multiple all over the body.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Anantapur, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter petitioner was shifted to Omega Multi Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Rapthadu Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.23/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Rapthadu Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 23/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P.1 to 7 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending KSRTC Bus.

The Ex.P.6 (Spot Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus U/s.338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.4 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
15. In order to rebut the claim of the petitioner, respondent examined CMO, Government General Hospital, Ananthpuram, Andhra Pradesh as RW.1 and he produced the documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.

He depose that, on 14.01.2023 petitioner came to the hospital with history of RTA at 10 p.m., and the petitioner was conscious and also examine the driver of the said KSRTC Bus as RW.2 Ramesh.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86331515/
4 and deposed that, on the date and time of the alleged accident in question was on its schedule trip from Bangalore to Ananthapur and the bus was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding on Bangalore-Ananthapur main road at Maruru cross at that point of time a motorcyclist abruptly darted the main road from the cross road, observing the same the driver of the bus, in order to avoid the bus being dashed against the motorcycle immediately stopped the bus and which has resulted in the minor incident.

16. In this case, learned counsel for respondent argued that, accident is not taken place due to the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, he argued that, petitioner has filed complaint after 14 days of the accident.

But on going through the materials available on record i.e.,
Wound Certificate at Ex.P.5, discharge summary at Ex.P.12, MLC report i.e., Ex.R.2 as well as evidence of RW.1 i.e., CMO, Government General Hospital, Ananthpur clearly shows that, the accident is taken place on 14.01.2023.
The said documents is not denied by the contesting respondents.

Further, respondent himself examine the CMO of Government General Hospital,
Ananthpura as RW.1.
In his chief examination itself he depose that, on 14.01.2023 petitioner visit this hospital with history of RTA at 10.00 p.m.,
So, these things itself goes to show that, petitioner sustained injury on 14.01.2023 itself.
It is true that, petitioner has filed complaint against the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus on 28.01.2023 i.e., after 14 days from the date of incident.
This tribunal opine that, treatment of the victim is given priority over lodging of FIR and delay of lodging of FIR cannot be ground to deny the justice to the claimants.

This view of this tribunal receives support from decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court as well as High Court which are reported in, 2022 ACJ 2482 between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Sahanaz Bibi and others, 2022 ACJ 170 between Venkatesha K. N Vs. Thipregowda and others and 2011 ACJ 2350 between Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation Vs. Pullaiah .

So, in view of above facts and circumstances,
delay caused in filing of the First Information before the concerned police does not itself dis-entitle the claim from the respondent.

17. In this case, petitioner was traveling as passenger in offending KSRTC Bus and he sustained injury when the offending vehicle hit the road side divider and Investigation officer has filed final report against the accused for the offense punishable U/s 338 of IPC and said final report is not challenged by the respondent.

18. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus Ramesh.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86331515/
5
bearing
Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

20. ISSUE No.2: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Government General Hospital, Anantapur, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter petitioner was shifted to Omega Multi Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and he took treatment.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
21. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government General Hospital, Anantapur, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter petitioner was shifted to Omega Multi Specialty Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary card marked at Ex.P.12, wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the hospital from 17.01.2023 to 22.01.2023 i.e., 05 days.
He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5, wherein the doctor has opined that, petitioner has sustained L2 fracture and the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 21 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.13 to the tune of Rs.1,46,420/-.

Further during the course of cross-examination of PW.1, counsel for respondent suggested to the petitioner that, medical bill at Sl. No.9 to 17 are xerox copies of the medical bills which do not have seal and signatures from the concerned hospital authorities.
On going through the medical at Sl. No.9 to 17 it can be seen that, no signature is affixed on the said bills and if we calculated the same it would come to Rs.2,122/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,44,298/- (after deducting the bills mentioned at Sl. No.9 to 17) towards medical expenses.

23. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.12 Discharge summary issued by Mega Multi-Specialty Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment in the said hospital from 17.01.2023 to 22.01.2023 i.e., 05 days.
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is the further contention that, the injured petitioner was doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/-
per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document.

Thus,
there is no cogent material on record to show actual income of the petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Hence, income of petitioner is to be fixed notionally.
It is pertinent to note that, Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority framed chart of notional income and directed to follow the same.

As per the said guidelines,
the fixed notional income for the year 2023 is at Rs.16,000/-.

sentences.text: Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.
24. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-
The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, this petitioner has disability of 20%.
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor.
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 20% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 14% of disability to the petitioner.
25. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.15 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his D.O.B is mentioned as 11.06.1990 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 33 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '16'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.4,30,080/-.

26. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Omega Multi-Specialty Hospital, Bangalore, as inpatient from 17.01.2023 to 22.01.2023 i.e., 05 days.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
27. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 33 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 1,44,298/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 32,000/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning, Rs. 4,30,080/-
Disability 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-

7 attendant charges 6

 happiness

Total Rs. 7,36,378/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,36,378/- under various heads.
28. LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-40-F-1336.
However, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurer of the offending KSRTC bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

29. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
30. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.7,36,378/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.

Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-40-F-1336.
12.
As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
It is true that, petitioner has filed complaint against the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus on 28.01.2023 i.e., after 14 days from the date of incident.
This tribunal opine that, treatment of the victim is given priority over lodging of FIR and delay of lodging of FIR cannot be ground to deny the justice to the claimants.
So, in view of above facts and circumstances,
delay caused in filing of the First Information before the concerned police does not itself dis-entitle the claim from the respondent.
17. In this case, petitioner was traveling as passenger in offending KSRTC Bus and he sustained injury when the offending vehicle hit the road side divider and Investigation officer has filed final report against the accused for the offense punishable U/s 338 of IPC and said final report is not challenged by the respondent.
18. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
19 . In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.
Thus,
there is no cogent material on record to show actual income of the petitioner at the time of accident in question.
Hence, income of petitioner is to be fixed notionally.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 14% of disability to the petitioner.
25. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.

30. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.7,36,378/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.
Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
